title: Starlink: newly deployed satellites lost
summary: 38 of 49 satellites from the February 3 launch were lost after enhanced atmospheric drag prevented orbit raising.
mechanism: Storm-driven upper-atmosphere heating increased drag at very low deployment altitudes.
limit: This was a deployment loss, not a measured customer-service outage. It does not establish the failure rate of operational Starlink satellites.

title: ICESat-2: science collection paused
summary: Unexpected drag rotated ICESat-2 and triggered safe hold, turning off its science instrument. NASA reported no detectable hardware damage.
mechanism: Expansion of the upper atmosphere increased orbital drag.
limit: A protective safe hold is an operational interruption, not destruction of the spacecraft.

title: GPS-guided agriculture: positioning disrupted
summary: NASA reports that some GPS-guided tractors veered off course or stopped working during the Gannon storm, disrupting planting.
mechanism: The disturbance affected satellite-based positioning used by receivers on the ground.
limit: Receiver or positioning problems do not mean that GPS satellites failed. This entry shares the May storm with ICESat-2; it is not another independent storm.

title: GPS: disturbance without significant system impact
summary: NGA described solar interference in navigation measurements but reported no significant impact to the GPS system from the October flare discussed in its report.
mechanism: Radio noise and ionospheric disturbances can affect signal tracking; system resilience and mitigation matter.
limit: This does not mean every receiver or location was unaffected. The source does not give an exact event day here.
